sentences.text: JUDGMENT
Since these four appeals arise out of the judgment and award, they are heard together and disposed of by this common judgment.

2. These appeals in MFA Nos.201907/2016 and MFA Crob.No.200034/2017 are filed challenging the judgment and award dated 18.07.2016 passed in MVC No.524/2013 and appeals in MFA No.201906/2016 and MFA Crob.No.200035/2017 are filed challenging the judgment and award dated 18.07.2016 passed in MVC No.523/2013 by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal').
3. Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants- petitioners submits that the Tribunal has committed a gross error in not considering any material evidence both oral and documentary and has awarded meager and inadequate compensation, which requires to be enhanced.

Further it is submitted that the petitioners were proceeding as unauthorized passengers in the offending vehicle Tractor and Trailer and the driver of the vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
The vehicle under the policy is insured with the agricultural tractor.
Therefore, there is no need and provision to carry the coolies on the said vehicle and thus the policy does not cover the risk.

Hence,
on these grounds and prays to allow the appeals filed by the petitioners and seeks to dismiss the appeals filed by the respondent-Insurance Company.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company supports the judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that there are no grounds to interfere with judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
He further submits that the tribunal has clearly discussed as to the liability of the Insurance Company and there is no reason to interfere with regard to liability of the Insurance Company.
Hence, on all these grounds prayed to allow the appeals filed by the respondent-Insurance Company and prayed to dismiss the appeals filed by the petitioners.

6. Heard the learned counsel for petitioners and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company.
7.
Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

8. The following points that arise for consideration before this court are :-
i) Whether the respondent-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the tribunal with regard to liability?
ii) Whether the petitioner in MVC No.523/2013 and 524/2013 are entitled for enhancement of compensation?

sentences.text:
My answers to the above points are:
Point No.1: Negative.
Point No.2: Partly affirmative.

Point No.3: As per final order.
10.
I have gone through the material placed by the petitioners.
11. It is not in dispute that petitioners have met with an accident that occurred on 04.02.2013 and sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

In order to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioners have produced copy of charge sheet which is marked as Ex.P3. Ex.P3, discloses that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent by the driver of the offending vehicle.
The insurance policy was valid and inforce at the time of accident as per Ex.R.4.

Though the respondent No.3 has examined the RW.1 to prove its - 10 - defence, this witness has stated that the offending vehicle driver is entitled to drive the tractor trolley on the basis of the DL issued for driving LMV Non Transport vehicle.
The RW.2 is cross-examination has clearly admitted the suggestion that the insurance policy was valid to the vehicle on the date of accident and that vehicle is purchased for the agricultural work.
The RW.3 in cross- examination has admitted the suggestion that he is the owner of the offending vehicle.

23. The learned counsel for the respondent No.3 drew my attention to the contention of the respondent No.2 taken in the objection with regard to the denial of the accident and travelling of the petitioner in the offending vehicle.

It is true that the respondent No.2 in the paragraph No.2 of the objection and his evidence affidavit has denied the fact of accident and the travelling of the petitioner in the tractor trolley ie., offending vehicle.

Therefore, the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submitted that since the owner himself has denied the accident and the travelling of the petitioner in the offending vehicle, the question of indemnifying him by this respondent No.3 does not arise.

sentences.text: It is necessary to say that though the respondent No.2 owner has denied so about the accident and the travelling of the petitioner in the offending vehicle, the said denial does not mean that the petitioner was not travelling in the offending vehicle and that the accident did not occur, because the oral as well as the documentary evidence including the complaint and charge sheet unmistakably establish that on 4-2-2013, the petitioner was travelling in the offending vehicle for going to the land of the - 11 - respondent No.2 for coolie work.

It is very necessary to say that though the respondent No.2 has denied the travelling of the petitioner in the offending vehicle on the date of accident, the respondent No.3 in paragraph No.7 of the written statement has clearly stated that on the date of CIVIL JU accident, the petitioner alongwith other 7 to 8 persons were travelling in the tractor and trailer i.e., offending vehicle of the respondent No. 2.
What it goes to show is that the petitioner and other 7 to 8 persons were really travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
But it is further contended that they were unauthorized passengers.
This contention is not proved by the respondents.

Merely because, the respondent No.2 has denied the alleged accident and the travelling of the petitioner in the offending vehicle, it does not mean that the petitioner was not travelling in the offending vehicle on that day for going to the land of the respondent No.2 as a coolie.

Therefore, keeping in mind the above referred decisions relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioner, I have to come to conclusion that petitioner was travelling in the offending vehicle for going to the respondent No.2's land for coolie work, but not as an unauthorized passenger.

This Claims Tribunal in MVC No.502/2013 as per Ex.R.5 and Ex.R.6 has already held the respondents No.2 and 3 as liable to pay the compensation to the injured petitioners who sustained the injuries in the same accident.

Under such circumstances, it is the respondents No.2 and 3 who are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation, because the respondent No.3 has failed to prove the violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.2.

Therefore, the respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner - 12 - with cost and interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the realization of entire compensation amount.
Since it is the liability of the respondent No.3 to indemnify the respondent No.2, it has to deposit the entire compensation amount with cost and interest.

So,
considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence, 1 have to say that the petitioner is entitled for the above said compensation, but not so much as claimed in the claim petition.
Since the respondent No.1 is the driver, this case against him shall be dismissed.

Accordingly, I have answered the issue No.2 partly in the AFFIRMATIVE.
13.
The tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.

Apart from this, the Investigating Officer has not submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the commission of offence punishable under Section 3 r/w 181 of M.V.Act and Section 5 r/w 180 of M.V. Act.
The Investigating Officer has also not submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle under Section 66 r/w 192A of M.V.Act.

Viewed from any Sushma D/O Revansiddappa Anakal vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd And Ors on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43835887/
8 angle, the Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability. Accordingly, the tribunal has properly held that the - 13 - Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer point No.1 in the negative.
14. IN MFA No.201907/2016 and MFA Crob.No.200034/2017 arising out of MVC No.524/2013:
Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and loss of future earning capacity due to disability.
Admittedly, age of the petitioner is 19 years.
The income assessed by the tribunal at Rs.4,500/- per month is on the lower side.
Admittedly there is no material proof of income.

As per the notional income chart prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2013 the income has to be taken at Rs.7,000/- per month and same is taken into consideration.
The age of the petitioner was 19 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 18 which is rightly taken and same is not interfered.

15. The petitioner has also got examined the Doctor as PW.2 who was deposed before the Court by stating that the petitioner has disability of 21% to the whole body, the - 14 - Tribunal has taken the evidence of the expert into consideration and has rightly assessed the disability to the whole body at 7%.
I do not find any legal impediment and illegality or perversity in the order passed by the Tribunal in assessing the disability to the whole body and hence the same is not disturbed and retained.

IN MFA No.201906/2016 C/w MFA Crob.No.200035/2017 arising out of MVC No.523/2013:
Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and loss of future earning capacity due to disability.
Admittedly, age of the petitioner is 35 years.
The income assessed by the tribunal at Rs.4,500/- per month is on the lower side.
Admittedly there is no material proof of income.

As per the notional income chart prescribed by the Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2013 the income has to be taken at Rs.7,000/-
- 15 - per month and same is taken into consideration.

The age of the petitioner was 35 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 16 which is rightly taken and same is not interfered.
17.

The petitioner has also got examined the Doctor as PW.2 who was deposed before the Court by stating that the petitioner has disability of 12% to the whole body, 1/3rd of which comes to 4% hence the disability assessed by the tribunal is just and proper.

Accordingly, the loss of future earning capacity due to disability would be;

For the aforesaid reasons and discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
- 17 - ORDER (a) The appeal filed by the petitioners in MFA Crob.
Nos.200034/2017 and 200035/2017 are allowed in part.
(b) The appeal filed by the respondent-Insurance Company in MFA No.201907/2016 and MFA No.201906/2016 are dismissed.
(c) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
(d) The petitioner in MVC No.524/2013 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,84,535/- as against Rs.1,33,235/- awarded by the tribunal.
(e) The petitioner in MVC No.523/2013 is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,17,260/- as against Rs.85,418/- awarded by the tribunal.

(f) The petitioners in both cases are entitled for compensation along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of amount.
(g) The respondent Nos.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
(h) Respondent No.3, Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount - 18 - along with interest, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(i) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
(j) The amount in deposit if any shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
(k) Registry is directed to send the copy of the judgment along with TCR to the concerned tribunal forthwith.

8. The following points that arise for consideration before this court are :-
i) Whether the respondent-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the tribunal with regard to liability?
ii) Whether the petitioner in MVC No.523/2013 and 524/2013 are entitled for enhancement of compensation?

My answers to the above points are:
Point No.1: Negative.
11. It is not in dispute that petitioners have met with an accident that occurred on 04.02.2013 and sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.
12. With regard to liability is concerned, in paragraph Nos.22 to 24 of the impugned judgment the tribunal has observed as under;
22. LIABILITY OF PAYMENT OF COMPENSATION:
In so far as liability to pay the compensation is concemed, it is the specific contention of the petitioner and an admitted fact that the respondent No.1 is the driver, the respondent No.2 is the owner and the respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The insurance policy was valid and inforce at the time of accident as per Ex.R.4.
Merely because, the respondent No.2 has denied the alleged accident and the travelling of the petitioner in the offending vehicle, it does not mean that the petitioner was not travelling in the offending vehicle on that day for going to the land of the respondent No.2 as a coolie.
Under such circumstances, it is the respondents No.2 and 3 who are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation, because the respondent No.3 has failed to prove the violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner - 12 - with cost and interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the realization of entire compensation amount.
Since it is the liability of the respondent No.3 to indemnify the respondent No.2, it has to deposit the entire compensation amount with cost and interest.
So,
considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence, 1 have to say that the petitioner is entitled for the above said compensation, but not so much as claimed in the claim petition.
Since the respondent No.1 is the driver, this case against him shall be dismissed.
The tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.
Apart from this, the Investigating Officer has not submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the commission of offence punishable under Section 3 r/w 181 of M.V.Act and Section 5 r/w 180 of M.V. Act.
The Investigating Officer has also not submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle under Section 66 r/w 192A of M.V.Act.
Viewed from any Sushma D/O Revansiddappa Anakal vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd And Ors on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43835887/
8 angle, the Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability. Accordingly, the tribunal has properly held that the - 13 - Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.
Admittedly there is no material proof of income.
The age of the petitioner was 19 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 18 which is rightly taken and same is not interfered.
